package local

import (
	"context"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

type closeRecorder struct {
	io.Reader
	closed bool
}

func (body *closeRecorder) Close() error {
	body.closed = true
	return nil
}

// An http.RoundTripper closes the request body on every path, the
// canceled early return included.
func TestTransportClosesTheBody(t *testing.T) {
	handler := http.HandlerFunc(func(writer http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
		writer.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
	})
	for _, canceled := range []bool{false, true} {
		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
		if canceled {
			cancel()
		}
		body := &closeRecorder{Reader: strings.NewReader("{}")}
		request, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, "http://gofastr.local/notes", body)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		response, err := (transport{handler: handler}).RoundTrip(request)
		if err == nil {
			response.Body.Close()
		}
		cancel()
		if !body.closed {
			t.Errorf("canceled=%v: request body left open", canceled)
		}
	}
}

// A handler never gets a nil Body from net/http ("the Request Body is
// always non-nil"), so it does not get one from this transport either:
// a client request with nothing to send (a List, a Get, a Delete) reaches
// the app with an empty body. The bug: the request was dispatched as the
// client built it, and middleware that drains or closes r.Body on every
// request, correct over HTTP, hit a nil pointer under Local. The caller's
// own request is left as it was.
func TestTransportHandsTheHandlerABody(t *testing.T) {
	for _, method := range []string{http.MethodGet, http.MethodDelete} {
		var seen io.ReadCloser
		handler := http.HandlerFunc(func(writer http.ResponseWriter, request *http.Request) {
			seen = request.Body
			if request.Body != nil {
				_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, request.Body)
				_ = request.Body.Close()
			}
			writer.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
		})
		request, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(context.Background(), method, "http://gofastr.local/notes", nil)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		response, err := (transport{handler: handler}).RoundTrip(request)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: %v", method, err)
		}
		response.Body.Close()
		if seen == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: the handler got a nil Body", method)
		}
		if request.Body != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: the transport set a Body on the caller's request", method)
		}
	}
}
